$comment: The moments of the translation file, as sequences (moments.md is the prose). Each case is a list of acts on a fresh translation folder, then what the file and its companions must say. Acts: `download` {hash, site_id, lines} (the server's file replaces the local one), `edit` {key, v, t}, `remove` {key}, `write` (the file is written: the count is measured), `merge` {hash, published, merged} (published = the server's lines, may be null; merged = the result taken), `upload` {hash, site_id}, `main_merge` {hash, lines} (a branch took its Main), `fork` {uuid, resolved_lines, content_hash}, `load` (a fresh reader re-derives everything from the files). Facts: `uuid`, `source_hash`, `site_id`, `main_hash`, `local_changes`, `forked_from` (object or null), `ancestor` and `main_ancestor` (`absent`, or the exact lines). `held_by` names the executors: `mod` (Core.Checks/TranslationStoreChecks over Engine/TranslationStore) and `manager` (Manager.Core.Checks/MomentsContractChecks over Install/TranslationInstaller); a side skips a case it does not hold and says so.

cases.why: the file is the server's: its hash is what this machine has now seen, the row is remembered (what lets a mod with nobody signed in ask the public check), nothing is local yet, and the ancestor is the file itself — the two sides provably agree at this instant
leaving a count inherited from whoever uploaded it would make the mod believe the player had edits they never made, and offer to merge them
a changed line and a new line are two things still to publish; the ancestor does not move on an edit, only on a sync
walking only the local lines made deletions invisible: the count stayed at zero, 'in sync' was judged true, and the divergence read as a SERVER update that would have restored what the player deleted

an interface line the server's copy holds and this file no longer does was published by a version that kept the mod's interface inside the game's translation; taking it out is this version doing what it must, not work waiting to be shared

three facts: the hash is the PUBLISHED version's (now seen, whether or not all of it was kept); the ancestor is the PUBLISHED content, never the merged one (what the two sides last agreed on is what was published — the merged file as ancestor would make the kept line look like common ground and the next merge would drop it); the count is what the merged file has that the published one does not — the one line still to publish
with only the result in hand there is no published content to name; the merged lines stand as the baseline, which claims nothing beyond what was actually seen
what was just sent IS what the site now holds: the ancestor is the local file as sent, the hash is the one the site answered, nothing is left to publish
an answer that names no row is not a row lost
the Main goes into ITS ancestor, never into ours: the two baselines answer different questions (what did the Main last look like / what did my own line last agree on) and must not mix

a new lineage: where it came from is written down before the reset wipes the sync state, every line is now local, and BOTH ancestors are deleted — a lineage left has no common ground with the one joined (the moment that did not happen for months, when the clean-up looked for a misspelt file)
a fresh file carries no _source, no _forked_from and no _local_changes: absent is the written form of 'nothing to say'
a fresh reader over the written file and its ancestor lands on the same facts — nothing about the file lives only in memory, and nothing of a previous file survives a load
